samples.question: The picture shows a plain background, a cloud of many small grey dots, and four straight coloured bars - one red, one green, one blue and one orange - lying near the edges of the picture, outside the cloud. Every grey dot has the same size and the same colour, and no single dot carries any meaning: only the shape of the whole cloud matters. The cloud is stretched further along one straight direction than along any other direction, and that direction is the cloud's long axis. The long axis is not drawn. Exactly one of the four bars points more nearly along the cloud's long axis than the other three bars do; a bar's direction is the direction of the straight bar itself, and a direction and its opposite count as the same direction. The colours of the bars, where each bar sits, how long or thick the bars are, how many dots there are and how much ink the picture contains all carry no information. Which coloured bar points most nearly along the cloud's long axis? Answer red, green, blue or orange.
